If enforcement narrows the effective buyer pool for certain SKUs, the remaining domestic demand could bid up spot rates, particularly for the high-end Hopper and Blackwell parts.
- **Large committed deployments.** The SpaceX $43 billion Nvidia GPU deal, the Argentum AI / Kyndryl $630 million collaboration, and Lambda's 10,000-GPU photonics cluster all lock in substantial volumes of Hopper- and Blackwell-class silicon. Committed capacity that is not available on the open market can tighten the residual on-demand supply.
- **Equity-market signal.** NVDA closed at $151.16, down 8.4 % on the day, 37.9 % below the 52-week high of $243.37, 21.4 % above the 52-week low of $124.5, and -18.76 % year-to-date versus the prior year-end close. The sharp single-day declines in both names could signal a near-term pullback in capex sentiment, which would be a *downward* force on GPU rental pricing if it translates into deferred data-centre build-outs.

- **Measurement-methodology shifts.** Multiple SKUs (B200, H200, H100 SXM, A100 80 GB, A100 40 GB, L40S, L4, MI300X, RTX 4090, RTX 5090, T4, A100 PCIe) had their on-demand measurement changed in August or November 2026 – most notably the switch from the single cheapest offer to the 25th percentile of ≥ 3 offers, and the pinning of memory size (40 GB A100s no longer published as 80 GB).
